1. Identified all infrastructure entities from the visual World Model and transcript: NLB, HAProxy EC2 Auto Scaling group, ELB (TCP mode), App EC2 tier, RDS Primary (Master), and RDS Secondary (Slave).
2. Pruned generic user human actor as per Node Rule 5, starting system entry point at NLB.
3. Normalized node service names against the valid vocabulary (NLB, EC2, ELB, RDS).

graph.name: Logicworks HIPAA-Compliant Architecture on AWS
graph.notes: A HIPAA-compliant architecture designed for heavily regulated environments, handling fixed IP whitelist requirements using NLB, 10,000+ SSL cert terminations using HAProxy on EC2, TCP-mode ELB pass-through, and RDS master-slave setup.

nodes.name: NLB
nodes.notes: Provides fixed public IP addresses per public subnet for client egress firewall whitelisting.

nodes.name: HAProxy EC2
nodes.notes: Auto Scaling cluster running HAProxy to handle SSL termination for 10,000+ certificates.

nodes.name: ELB
nodes.notes: Elastic Load Balancer operating in TCP mode to pass through encrypted traffic to the application tier.

nodes.name: App EC2
nodes.notes: Application layer running inside an EC2 Auto Scaling compute tier.

nodes.name: RDS Primary
nodes.notes: Primary database instance (master) serving core application reads and writes.

nodes.name: RDS Secondary
nodes.notes: Secondary database instance (slave) used for master-slave replication and reporting workloads.

edges.notes: NLB routes incoming external requests down to the HAProxy EC2 cluster.
HAProxy terminates SSL and forwards requests to the internal ELB.
ELB passes TCP traffic to the App EC2 cluster.
App instances query and write data to the Primary RDS database instance.
Replicating data from RDS Primary to RDS Secondary for high availability and reporting.
